module_title: Motherboard Architecture - System Buses, Legacy Ports, and Expansion Slots
introduction: This intermediate tier delves into the internal layout of the motherboard. We will classify the System Bus into its technical sub-types, examine legacy ports that frequently appear in historical computing questions, and understand expansion slots.

core_concepts.title: The 3 Types of System Buses
core_concepts.description:
1. Data Bus: Carries the actual raw data back and forth (Bidirectional).
2. Address Bus: Carries the specific memory location/address where data needs to be sent or fetched (Unidirectional - outward from CPU).
3. Control Bus: Carries command and timing signals (like Read/Write) from the Control Unit.

core_concepts.title: Legacy Ports
core_concepts.description:
- PS/2 Port: Old 6-pin round ports (Green for Mouse, Purple for Keyboard).
- Serial Port (RS-232): A 9-pin port used for old dial-up modems and mice. Transmits data one bit at a time (slow).
- Parallel Port (LPT): A long 25-pin port traditionally used to connect older printers and scanners. Transmits multiple bits simultaneously.

core_concepts.title: RJ-45 (Ethernet/LAN Port)
core_concepts.description: An 8-pin port used to connect the computer to a wired Local Area Network (LAN) or a router for internet access. It looks like a telephone jack but is noticeably wider.

core_concepts.title: Expansion Slots
core_concepts.description: Empty slots built into the motherboard allowing users to add 'Expansion Cards' (like dedicated Graphics Cards, Sound Cards, or Wi-Fi cards). The historical standard was 'PCI' (Peripheral Component Interconnect), now replaced by the modern 'PCIe' (PCI Express).

important_entities.name: CMOS Battery
important_entities.significance: A small coin-cell battery on the motherboard (Complementary Metal-Oxide Semiconductor) that powers the BIOS memory chip, ensuring the system clock and hardware settings are saved even when the PC is unplugged.

important_entities.name: DIMM Slots
important_entities.significance: DIMM (Dual In-line Memory Module) slots are the long, narrow sockets on the motherboard where the primary memory (RAM sticks) are physically installed.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A very frequent question asks: 'Which legacy port was primarily used to connect older printers?' Options usually include Serial and Parallel. The correct answer is strictly the 'Parallel Port' (LPT).
Examiners test the strict color coding of the legacy PS/2 ports. Do not swap them: Green = Mouse | Purple = Keyboard.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember the three system buses using the acronym DAC: Data, Address, Control.

exam_strategy_tips: In banking mains and SSC Tier-2, questions frequently contrast Serial vs. Parallel data transmission. Remember that Parallel is faster over short distances (like printers) because it sends multiple bits at once.
